A black squall wall stands along the far horizon with a burning saffron gap beneath it, the standing water repeating both, saffron streaks cut by blue-black hollows.
Bruised lobed mammatus hang low and violet over the flats, acid-chartreuse light raking the wet sand between them, the shallows below holding violet above and chartreuse underfoot.
A double rainbow stands on the horizon and plants its feet in the water, one arc overhead in tangerine and teal, one arc below reversed in the sheen.
Pre-dawn rose bleeds down into deep indigo at the zenith, the wet mirror carrying rose low across the flats, indigo pooled in every hollow cut through it.
A rain curtain hangs translucent on the right with the sun blazing coral behind it, the left sky a hard prussian blue, the standing water splitting both colours across the flat.
High feathered cirrus catches coral light overhead while the lower sky holds cold turquoise, the sheen below repeating coral streaks above turquoise between the dark water-filled hollows.
A sun-dog blazes on the left in a pillar of hot magenta, the surrounding sky a deep prussian blue, the standing water carrying the magenta pillar down across the flat.
Blue hour settles overhead while a single band of hot vermilion burns along the horizon, the wet surface below splitting into cold blue above and vermilion below, hollows dark.
A distant volcanic plume glows cherry-red from eruption light below, the sky around it a deep bruised violet, the standing water carrying the cherry column across the flat.
A waxing moon hangs in a still-bright teal sky banded with hot apricot along the horizon, the sheen below holding teal wide and apricot pooled in every hollow.
Scattered cumulus cross the sky, each one bellied peach above and shadowed deep indigo beneath, the shallows doubling every cloud, hollows punching dark gaps through the pattern.
A fork of lightning splits a violet wall on the right horizon, the left sky a sick sulphur-yellow, the standing water repeating violet on one side and sulphur on the other.
The sun's disc sits exactly on the horizon, a flat disc of molten copper repeated disc-for-disc in the sheen below, slate-blue filling every ripple shadow between the two discs.
A green squall-light floods the sky from horizon to zenith, the cloud base a rotting purple-grey, the standing water below divided into green sheen and dark purple in every hollow.
Hail-light pours through a break in a cloud base of deep bruised plum, the flat below blazing acid-lime under the break and plum-dark everywhere else.
The low sun rakes from the left, burning sienna along every ripple crest, cold lavender pooled in every ripple trough, the wet mirror below doubling both stripes across the flat.
A towering cumulonimbus anvil spreads in deep violet-blue, its lit crown burning a fierce apricot, the standing water repeating violet wide and apricot where the crown falls.
Thin lenticular cloud glows a deep rose-crimson at the edges and grades to pale ash at the centre, the sheen below carrying crimson at the margins and ash between the hollows.
A light pillar stands vertical above the low sun in a column of peach-pink, the sky beside it a hard cobalt, the standing water repeating peach on one axis and cobalt across the rest.

Cirrostratus spreads a halo around a high sun in spectral ice-blue, the surrounding sky bleached to straw-yellow, the shallows below holding ice-blue in the halo's reflection and straw in the flat between.
A squall's rain curtain advances from the right in blue-grey veils, the far left sky still a vivid umber from the low sun, the wet surface splitting umber from blue-grey down the middle.
Mammatus in bruised ochre-brown hang across the upper frame, the lit gap below the cloud base a sharp electric cyan, the water repeating ochre above and cyan underfoot, hollows black.
A roll cloud stretches bank to bank in deep plum, a narrow slot of burning cadmium below it, the standing water repeating plum above and cadmium along the horizon's reflection.
Altocumulus castellanus rises in turrets of steel-blue and cream against a deep rust sky, the sheen below carrying rust across the flat and steel-blue in every cloud-shadow hollow.
The zenith is a hard prussian blue fading to a scorched terracotta at the horizon, the wet surface below reversing the gradient, terracotta near and prussian blue deep in the far hollows.
